record.paper_title: Open problems in deformations of Artinian algebras, Hilbert schemes and around
record.original_question: For every smoothable finite scheme Spec(A) of degree d, does there exist a completely split abstract smoothing over k[[t]] whose approximation degree is at most d? More weakly, does there exist a polynomial P such that one can always achieve approximation degree at most P(d)?

evidence.quote: Problem XXXVII. Is it true that for every smoothable finite scheme Spec(A) of degree d there exists a completely split abstract smoothing A of A with approximation degree at most d? Less restrictively, does there exist a polynomial P such that for every A as above there exists an A with approximation degree bounded by P(d)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, and let $A$ be a finite local $k$-algebra of $k$-vector-space dimension $d$, so that $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is a finite scheme of degree $d$ supported at a single point. Assume $A$ is smoothable, meaning that $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ lies in the closure of the locus of $d$ reduced points inside the Hilbert scheme of $d$ points.

An abstract smoothing of $A$ over $k[[t]]$ is a flat $k[[t]]$-algebra $\mathcal{A}$, finite of rank $d$, such that $\mathcal{A}/(t)\cong A$ and $\mathcal{A}\otimes_{k[[t]]} k((t))$ is a product of separable field extensions of $k((t))$. The smoothing is called completely split if $\mathcal{A}\otimes_{k[[t]]} k((t))\cong k((t))^{d}$. The approximation degree of such a smoothing is the smallest integer $N\ge 0$ such that the isomorphism class of $\mathcal{A}$ (as a flat $k[[t]]$-algebra deformation of $A$) is determined by its reduction modulo $t^{N+1}$; equivalently, the smallest $N$ such that any flat deformation of $A$ over $k[t]/(t^{N+1})$ extending the given one lifts uniquely (up to isomorphism) to a flat deformation over $k[[t]]$ realizing $\mathcal{A}$.

Question (strong form): For every smoothable finite local $k$-algebra $A$ of degree $d$, does there exist a completely split abstract smoothing $\mathcal{A}$ of $A$ over $k[[t]]$ whose approximation degree is at most $d$?

Question (weak form): Does there exist a polynomial $P(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$, independent of $A$, such that for every smoothable finite local $k$-algebra $A$ of degree $d$ there exists a completely split abstract smoothing of $A$ over $k[[t]]$ with approximation degree at most $P(d)$?
artifact.category_tag: Deformations of Artinian algebras and Hilbert schemes
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems on deformations of Artinian algebras and Hilbert schemes. Web searches turned up only related literature on smoothability and components of Hilbert schemes of points, with no result establishing either the linear bound $d$ or any polynomial bound $P(d)$ on the approximation degree of completely split abstract smoothings. No resolution appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Components of Hilbert Schemes of low degree and smoothable algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to investigate smoothability of finite algebras and components of Hilbert schemes of points.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on smoothable Artinian algebras continues, but no bound on approximation degree of smoothings is established.

status_evidence.title: Explicit deformation of a spider algebra to a curvilinear scheme via Möbius generators
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs explicit smoothings of certain Artinian algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit smoothing constructions exist in special cases but do not resolve the general approximation-degree bound.
